items.title: Gerald Wilson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: He doesn’t play like his father – he plays like Robbie

ctx.x: So many good people from Detroit.

Yeah, well you know, she know’s – you know, they know how to do these chords, they have these chords, and I wonder, why these are like that, but there’s a reason to have these certain notes in this chord. You know, so I studied that – I studied his music, I studied Coltrane’s music, and Alice. And incidentally, I like Robbie Coltrane. He’s a fine player, he’s a fine player. He doesn’t play like his father – he plays like Robbie, he plays like Robbie. As I said, there’s so many fine musicians now. As I said, I…
